answer: Each agent may open a claim only by locking a scarce, time-bound deposit, while a trellis of independent peers checks its signed actions against the same public history. Reusing one identity across claims risks slashing the deposit when conflicting behavior is proven; creating many identities requires funding each lock and keeping them active through review. A plume of fabricated accounts therefore cannot vote cheaply: the attacker must tie up real capital for the full voyage and may lose it on equivocation.
